Copper cost of sales per pound is calculated as cost of sales across our copper operations divided by pounds sold (both on an attributable basis using Barrick’s ownership share). da.text: EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial performance measure, which excludes the following from net earnings: income tax expense; finance costs; finance income; and depreciation. Management believes that EBITDA is a valuable indicator of our ability to generate liquidity by producing operating cash flow to fund working capital needs, service debt obligations, and fund capital expenditures. Management uses EBITDA for this purpose. Adjusted EBITDA removes the effect of impairment charges; acquisition/disposition gains/losses; foreign currency translation gains/losses; and other expense adjustments. We also remove the impact of the income tax expense, finance costs, finance income and depreciation incurred in our equity method accounted investments. We believe these items provide a greater level of consistency with the adjusting items included in our adjusted net earnings reconciliation, with the exception that these amounts are adjusted to remove any impact on finance costs/income, income tax expense and/or depreciation as they do not affect EBITDA.

cor.text: In Q3 2026, gold cost of sales on a consolidated basis was 1% lower than Q2 2026, primarily due to lower unit costs as described below. Our 45% interest in Kibali and 24.5% interest in Porgera are equity accounted, and therefore each mine’s cost of sales is excluded from our consolidated gold cost of sales. Our per ounce metrics, gold COS/oz 2 and TCC/oz 1 , include our proportionate share of cost of sales at our equity method investees, and were 2% and 3% lower, respectively, compared to Q2 2026 primarily driven by changes in the sales mix across the portfolio, the shutdown activity in Q2 2026 and the impact of lower royalties due to a lower realized gold price 1 .

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
General and administrative expenses for Q3 2026 increased by $20 million compared to Q2 2026 due to higher share-based compensation driven by an increase in our share price, combined with higher corporate administration expenses primarily due to higher labour and external services costs.

For Q3 2026 and YTD 2026, general and administrative expenses decreased by $26 million and $37 million compared to Q3 2025 and YTD 2025, respectively, mainly due to lower share-based compensation expenses, reflecting lower share price appreciation in Q3 2026 compared to Q3 2025 and a decline in our share price during YTD 2026 compared to an increase in YTD 2025.

nonop.text: For Q3 2026 and YTD 2026, finance costs, net were lower than the prior year periods, mainly due to higher interest capitalized, primarily relating to Reko Diq and Lumwana, partially offset by higher interest expense. Q3 2026 was further impacted by lower finance income.

tax.text: Consistent with the amendments to IAS 12 Income Taxes issued by the IASB in May 2023, the Group has applied the mandatory temporary exception from the recognition and disclosure of deferred tax assets and liabilities arising from Pillar Two income taxes. Accordingly, no deferred tax assets or liabilities have been recognized or disclosed in respect of Pillar Two legislation.

net.text: Since it was consolidated from December 16, 2025, Loulo-Gounkoto contributed revenue of $505 million and net income of $16 million for the year ended December 31, 2025. If the acquisition had occurred on January 1, 2025, consolidated revenue and consolidated net income for the year ended December 31, 2025, would have been $1,036 million and $484 million, respectively. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue and net income were $1,441 million and $587 million, respectively, and excludes other expenses relating to additional royalties, penalties and interest paid to the Government of Mali due to the retrospective application of the 2023 Mining Code to 2024 and 2025. Refer to note 9 for further details. The fair value of accounts receivable was $104 million (included in other current assets) as at December 16, 2025, which was equivalent to the contractual amount.

ocf.text: Free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure that deducts capital expenditures from net cash provided by operating activities. Attributable free cash flow starts with free cash flow and adds our attributable share of free cash flow from our equity investees and subtracts the free cash flow attributable to the non-controlling interests. Management believes these to be useful indicators of our ability to operate without reliance on additional borrowing or usage of existing cash.

da.text: COS/oz 2 for YTD 2026 was 14% higher than YTD 2025, mainly reflecting higher depreciation associated with the Arturo open pit. TCC/oz 1 for YTD 2026 was 3% higher than YTD 2025, primarily driven by higher diesel prices, tariffs and higher royalties due to the higher realized gold price 1 . For YTD 2026, AISC/oz 1 was 2% lower than YTD 2025 driven by lower minesite sustaining capital expenditures 1 , partially offset by higher TCC/oz 1 .

sbc.text: General and administrative expenses for Q3 2026 increased by $20 million compared to Q2 2026 due to higher share-based compensation driven by an increase in our share price, combined with higher corporate administration expenses primarily due to higher labour and external services costs.

wc.text: We believe we have sufficient financial resources to meet our business requirements for the foreseeable future, including capital expenditures, working capital requirements, interest payments, environmental rehabilitation, share buybacks and dividends.

capex.text:
Capital expenditures are classified into minesite sustaining capital expenditures or project capital expenditures depending on the nature of the expenditure. Minesite sustaining capital expenditures is the capital spending required to support current production levels. Project capital expenditures represent the capital spending at new projects and major, discrete projects at existing operations intended to increase net present value through higher production or longer mine life. Management believes this to be a useful indicator of the purpose of capital expenditures

and this distinction is an input into the calculation of all-in sustaining costs per ounce/pound.

fcf.text: The Company’s dividend policy targets a total payout of 50% of attributable free cash flow 1 on an annualized basis, comprised of a fixed base quarterly dividend of $0.175 per share and a performance top-up component at each year end based on the attributable free cash flow during the year. The dividend paid in any given year may be higher or lower than the 50% target based on the strength of cash flow, capital needs, balance sheet considerations, and other factors.

net sales.text: In Q3 2026, gold revenues on a consolidated basis decreased by 4% compared to Q2 2026, driven by a lower realized gold price 1 , partially offset by higher sales volumes. The average market price for Q3 2026 was $4,262/oz, representing a 5% decrease versus the $4,506/oz average in Q2 2026. During Q3 2026, the gold price ranged from $3,960/oz to $4,697/oz, and closed the quarter at $4,176/ oz. Gold price volatility in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by economic and geopolitical concerns, in particular the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Provisions
lines.why: Obligations of uncertain timing or amount (warranties, restructuring, legal claims): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

intro.text: Barrick is a leading global mining, exploration and development company. With one of the largest portfolios of world-class and long-life gold and copper assets in the industry — including six of the world’s Tier One gold mines — Barrick’s operations and projects span 18 countries and five continents. Barrick is also the largest gold producer in the United States. We create real, long-term value for all stakeholders through responsible mining, strong partnerships and a disciplined approach to growth. Barrick shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol ‘B’ and on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol ‘ABX’.
